answer:
Review of lakehouse-iceberg (region eu-central-1). Only Finding 1 has been recorded. The other findings are not recorded unless you ask.

Finding 1 [high · Reliability · REL09-BP01] The S3 Tables bucket lakehouse-prod holds 140 Iceberg tables with backup set to "none" and cross-region replication off, while the RPO is 1440 minutes. REL09-BP01 asks you to identify all data that needs backup, or can be reproduced from sources, and to back it up so that recovery meets the RPO [S1]. The raw layer has no retention either (raw_layer_retention: none), so it cannot be rebuilt from older data.

Finding 2 [medium · Operational Excellence · OPS10-BP02] Glue failure_alerts is false and max_retries is 0, so a failed nightly job at 02:00 UTC raises no alert and is not retried. OPS10-BP02 asks for a defined process per alert, owned by an accountable team, for operational events [S6]. Real-time alarm notifications to the right people are also expected [S8].

Finding 3 [medium · Security · SEC08-BP03] Athena query_results_encrypted is false, and the tables use SSE-S3 only. Automating data-at-rest protection, including encryption of stored data, is the practice this maps to [S15]. Encrypting the query results and reviewing the key choice for the tables would close this gap.

Finding 4 [medium · Cost Optimization · COST04-BP05] The raw layer has no retention policy, so source extracts accumulate indefinitely. COST04-BP05 asks you to define data retention and lifecycle policies that delete objects no longer required [S28].

Finding 5 [medium · Sustainability · SUS04-BP03] The same missing raw-layer retention also breaks the lifecycle practice. SUS04-BP03 asks you to manage dataset lifecycles and automatically enforce deletion, to minimise the storage the workload needs [S27].

No gap found in what was retrieved for Performance Efficiency. Iceberg compaction is enabled and the snapshot expiration is 7 days. The retrieved text on PERF03-BP04 asks for partitioning, columnar file formats and compression [S17]. The architecture does not state these settings, so I cannot confirm them either way. Athena also has no per-query bytes-scanned cutoff. The retrieved chunks do not cover that setting, so I cite no best practice for it.
